requirements.title: Design token layer (color roles, type scale, spacing, radius) replacing the create-next-app globals

sources.ref: Design direction: Space & shape, Color roles

requirements.requirement: One token file defines neutral surfaces (page, surface, raised, line, text, muted), one accent, five status roles (success, warning, danger, info, neutral), the type scale, a 4px spacing grid and three radii, in globals.css and the Tailwind v4 theme. The starter :root/prefers-color-scheme block and the white body background are removed.
acceptance: globals.css contains no create-next-app starter tokens; body background is the dark page token in both OS light and dark mode.
Tokens exist for page/surface/raised/line/text/muted, one accent, and success/warning/danger/info/neutral (text, soft fill, chip), each status text value ≥4.5:1 on the page and surface tokens.
Type tokens 12/13/14/16/20/24/28–32px, spacing 4/8/12/16/24/32/48, radii 6 (controls), 10 (cards), full (chips) are defined; rounded-[2rem]/rounded-3xl hero radii are retired as screens migrate.
Stage S0 (tokens reproducing today's palette) shows zero pixel diff on the 12 reference screens before any visual change ships.
Hex literal, rgb() and bg-white counts in src/app do not increase (ratchet, MOD-OPS-013).
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: Replace AppearanceStyleOverrides class-rewriting with token-driven theming
requirements.requirement: Agency appearance (brightness, contrast, accent) is applied by setting CSS variables on the shell root instead of [class*=…] !important overrides, so hover variants are never matched, translucent surfaces keep their opacity, the accent never recolors status colors, and the accent is applied before first paint.
acceptance: With balanced and high-contrast brightness, the computed background of an inactive nav link differs from the active link (component/visual test).
A unit test asserts no theming selector matches hover:, group-hover: or other variant classes.
Translucent slate surfaces (e.g. bg-slate-900/70) keep their opacity under every appearance mode.
The emerald accent does not change success/status colors, and the slate accent does not make primary buttons look disabled.
No hydration mismatch warning and no accent flash on first paint (accent set via cookie or pre-hydration script).

requirements.title: High contrast as a per-user display preference
requirements.screen: Settings > Branding > Screen brightness; user menu
requirements.requirement: Officers can turn on high contrast for themselves (daylight use) without changing the agency-wide appearance; the agency setting remains the default.
acceptance: A per-user High contrast toggle is available from the user menu and applies only to that user.
The agency-wide brightness setting is unchanged for other users after one user toggles it.
If the preference must roam across devices, the storage endpoint is delivered by the deployment team first (track C); a per-browser preference is acceptable for the first release.
requirements.notes: Appendix E finding; listed here because the theme is part of the token layer. Administration may also reference E-19 for the Settings screen.

requirements.title: Legible type: 12px floor, sentence-case labels, mono identifiers, data brighter than labels

sources.ref: Measured evidence: Text at 9–11px, Uppercase share, Letter-spacing

requirements.requirement: Nothing renders below 12px; labels are sentence case at 13px muted; uppercase is reserved for table headers (11px, one letter-spacing value); serials, asset tags, plates, scores and counts use Geist Mono with tabular figures; data is one step larger and brighter than its label. Module screens adopt the rule as they migrate.
acceptance: Count of text-[≤11px] in src/app falls to 0 outside table headers, and never increases in CI (ratchet).
One letter-spacing token replaces the 8 values (0.12–0.26em).
Uppercase share of visible text is <10% on each migrated screen (measured with the VR method).
Serials, plates, asset tags and scores render in the mono token with tabular numerals.
40 h1 elements collapse to the single PageHeader title style.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: Secondary and hint text meets 4.5:1 contrast
requirements.requirement: Hint and secondary text uses at least the muted token (slate-400 equivalent); the 37 slate-600/700 hint uses and the faint small text on Qualifications, Help, Range Days, Analytics and Dashboard are corrected as each screen migrates.
acceptance: axe color-contrast passes (≥4.5:1) on every migrated screen in the default dark theme.
No slate-600/700 text on slate-900/950 backgrounds remains in src/app (grep ratchet).
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: Flattened layout: cards only for objects, never card inside card
requirements.requirement: Cards are used only for things (a vehicle, a range day, an alert); sections are plain areas with a heading and divider; field lists are two-column definition lists without boxes; elevation comes from surface tone rather than borders.
acceptance: No migrated screen nests a bordered/rounded card inside another card (review checklist plus a lint rule or DOM probe in the visual-regression run).
Field lists on record pages render as definition lists without per-field boxes.

requirements.title: Five page templates: List, Record, Dashboard, Form/Wizard, Settings
requirements.requirement: Shared templates fix the order of every screen (what needs action, then the summary, then the detail), one primary action per view in the header or a sticky footer, 24px desktop / 16px phone gutter and 32px section gap. List = header, optional KPI strip, filter bar, table/cards, side drawer; Record = header with status, facts grid, tabs, activity; Dashboard = action list, KPIs, module cards; Form = two-column fields with sticky footer; Settings = left rail plus form panel.
acceptance: Each template exists as a composable layout with a gallery example.
Every migrated screen uses exactly one template and shows at most one primary button.
Shell owns page padding: no page adds its own px-6 py-8 inside the shell (no double gutters at 375px).

requirements.title: PageHeader component (breadcrumb, title, status chip, one primary, overflow)

It replaces the ~8 header patterns and ~20 title styles; the unused ArmoryPageHeader is either the seed or deleted.
acceptance: PageHeader has unit and accessibility tests and a gallery entry for every variant.
Title text comes from the route → nav metadata map, so it equals the menu label; eyebrows never contradict the menu.
Header height is consistent across migrated screens; no screen shows its title twice.
After adoption on R1 screens, the count of distinct h1 class strings decreases and never increases (ratchet).
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: Button kit: four variants, two sizes, built-in busy state

sources.ref: Measured evidence: Filled-button heights, Primary button colors

Green and amber are never button colors. A SubmitButton wrapper disables itself and shows a busy state while its request is in flight, so one tap creates one record.
acceptance: Button and SubmitButton have unit and accessibility tests; labels never wrap at supported widths.
A second click on a SubmitButton while its request is pending sends no second request (component test).
Distinct button className strings and bg-blue-600 variants decrease with each migrated module and never increase (ratchet).
Module adoption that fixes specific double-submit defects (C-07, C-48, D-65) is tracked by those modules' requirements.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

acceptance: The registry covers every status enum used by firearms, equipment, fleet, qualifications, inbox and range; raw enum strings are never rendered (unit test over the enum lists).
The 12 local status/tone maps and 10 local Pill/Badge components fall to 0 as modules migrate; CI ratchet never lets them increase.
'Due soon' and 'Overdue' look identical across modules.
S0 stage reproduces today's colors (zero pixel diff) before tones are changed.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: KpiTile: one tile design, neutral at zero, linked, with loading and error states
requirements.requirement: One KpiTile (label, 28–32px number, one context line, optional trend) replaces three tile designs and rainbow icon squares. It is neutral by default, colored only when the value means attention is needed, links to the filtered list behind the number, and has skeleton and 'Data unavailable · Retry' states.
acceptance: A zero value renders neutral (no red/green/amber tint).
Every tile with a number renders as a link (or button) to its filtered list.
Loading renders a skeleton, never 0; failure renders 'Data unavailable' with Retry.
KPI grids size to the tile count (no empty grid slot) and use 2 columns below 640px, 4 above.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: AsyncState: loading is a skeleton, failure is 'Couldn't load · Retry', never a false all-clear
requirements.requirement: A shared AsyncState (loading / error with Retry / empty / stale-copy) means no screen shows 'No records', zero counts or a green all-clear while data is loading or after it failed to load. It consumes the development team's error and empty handling instead of inventing its own.
acceptance: Component tests: pending → skeleton with no counts or empty-state copy; rejected → 'Couldn't load' with a working Retry; resolved-empty → neutral empty state; stale copy → labelled as stale.
No migrated screen renders a success-toned empty state while loading or after a load failure (visual regression captures the loading and error states).
The error/empty contracts from SV-05, SV-06 and SV-15 are used unchanged.
Module instances (B-24, B-40, B-63, C-26, C-37, C-53, D-28) are fixed by their modules using this component.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: EmptyState with next step and optional first-run guide

acceptance: EmptyState has gallery entries for plain, with-action and first-run variants, and accessibility tests.
Empty states never use success styling.
Module first-run content (Equipment, Inventory, Certifications, Ammunition, Docs) is delivered by those modules.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: Field component: visible label, help text, inline error, correct id/htmlFor

Gallery shows default, help, required, error and disabled states.
Placeholder-only inputs in migrated screens fall to 0 (module instances tracked by modules).

acceptance: Component tests cover sort, column chooser, row link and card mode at 375px.

Forced min-w-[NNNpx] tables decrease and never increase (ratchet).

acceptance: At 375px no list shows more than one row of filter controls before data.

requirements.title: ConfirmDialog, ReasonDialog and accountable-change Sheet per the §1b confirmation policy

Routine reversible edits get no confirmation.
acceptance: Native confirm/prompt/alert count in src/app reaches 0 as modules migrate and never increases (ratchet).
ConfirmDialog text states the record and consequence (e.g. 'Affects 14 members').
The accountable-change Sheet shows 'Recorded in … history with your name and time'.
Reason fields that are required today stay required; no confirmation or approval step is added to or removed from a workflow by UI work.
Audit writes are unchanged: a before/after network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads for every action, and the audit export matches the baseline.

acceptance: Toasts are announced by screen readers (aria-live) and render above any open Dialog.
Success toasts appear only after the server confirms the action.
Local notice/message state files decrease as modules migrate.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

requirements.title: InlineStatus save indicator driven only by server acknowledgements

requirements.title: SegmentedControl and Checklist components with no default value
requirements.requirement: A ≥44px SegmentedControl (Pass / Defect / Critical / N/A) and a Checklist (progress, note only on a defect, sticky summary and Submit, missing-items list) built on the remediated InspectionChoiceControl, with no default value.
acceptance: No safety-relevant control is pre-set (nothing defaults to Pass or OK); required acknowledgments are answered individually and cannot be bulk-filled.
Submit stays disabled and lists what is missing until every required item is answered; the result and its status effect are shown before Submit.
'Mark remaining N as Pass' fills only unanswered, non-acknowledgment items.
Segments are ≥44px tall on touch and keyboard operable (radio-group semantics).
Uses the same payloads as UX-RB-2; inspection screen adoption is tracked by the Armory and Fleet groups.
requirements.notes: Component built and tested on the foundation branch; screen adoption, ratchets and visual-regression snapshots remain before Implemented.

axe passes with a visible label; clear button ≥40px with an accessible name.
Module adoption (C-15, C-28, B-23, D-63) is tracked by those modules.
